title: GILT FRAMED FRENCH PRINT & A S...
reason: Documented S.T. Gill / Tingle steel engraving (Victoria Illustrated, Sands & Kenny) in a period gilt frame plus a loose Gill-style coloured vignette that is worth far more if it proves to be an original; likely $150-300 with upside.
findings: The gilt-framed piece is not a generic French print: it is a steel engraving titled Approach to Richmond from North Bank of Yarra Yarra, lettered S.T. Gill del. at lower left (read), with an engraver's credit at lower right that is too blurred to read (the NGV records this plate as engraved by J. Tingle), and the imprint Published by Sands & Kenny, Melbourne & Sydney, 1856 (the NGV records the same inscription; the series is Victoria Illustrated, published 1857). Photos cannot show whether it is an original or a later reprint (Sands & McDougall reissued Gill plates c.1890); comparable single plates retail around $110-130 unframed. Frame looks like a period gilt gesso frame with a beaded inner slip and a cream and gilt mount. The lot also has a loose, unframed sheet carrying a hand-coloured vignette: two men in straw hats planting a vegetable bed beside a verandah cottage, with a long shed and a river with rowing boats behind. It is unsigned in the photos and is in a colonial manner that could be Gill (could be a coloured print, or possibly a watercolour), maker unconfirmed. The title's French print is not identifiable, so the title may be mixing up the two pieces.
condition: Frame has gilt and gesso losses along the top edge and left side with some corner wear. Print is toned with a little foxing (glass and backing not visible). Loose sheet is creased, foxed, discoloured and edge-worn with a ragged edge.
rescore_note: Real S.T. Gill and Tingle steel engraving from Victoria Illustrated (Sands & Kenny imprint read) in a period gilt frame with losses, plus a creased loose coloured vignette of unknown origin; dealers ask A$110 to A$165 for single Gill plates (antiqueprintmaproom.com Gill listings, seen 19/10/2026), so my estimate is $120 to $220 with a small chance the loose sheet is worth more.
